ety.text: From Middle English hes, from Old English his (“his; its”), from Proto-Germanic *hes (“of this”), genitive of Proto-Germanic *hiz (“this, this one”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱe-, *ḱey- (“this”). Cognate with Danish, Swedish, Norwegian, Icelandic hans (“his”). More at he; see also its.

senses.d: Belonging to him.
ex:
With that he put his ſpurres vnto his ſteed,
 With ſpeare in reſt, and toward him did fare,
 Like ſhaft out of a bow preuenting ſpeed.

senses.d: Belonging to a person of unspecified gender.
Its; belonging to it. (Now only when implying personification.)
ex:
In ſo moche that if any verbe be of the thyꝛde coniugation
 I ſet out all his rotes and tenſes[…]
My ſtomacke could not well reach ſo farre: it is very much troubled to come to an end of that which it takes for his neede.

senses.d: Used as a genitive marker in place of ’s after a noun, especially a masculine noun ending in -s, to express the possessive case.
ex: Ahab his mark
Sejanus his Fall

senses.d: That or those belonging to him; the possessive case of he, used without a following noun.
ex: This pen is his. These books are also his.
The decision was his to live with.

senses.d: His house or home.
ex: After our night out, I went back to his.

From Latin historicus (“historical”) + -al (forming adjectives denoting of or relating to). By surface analysis, history + -ical.

senses.d: Of, concerning, or in accordance with recorded history, (particularly) as opposed to legends, myths, and fictions.
ex: July 4, 1776, is a historic date. A great deal of historical research has been done on the events leading up to that day.
The historical works of Lord Macaulay and Edward Gibbon are in and of themselves historic.

senses.d: About history; depicting persons or events from history.
Of, concerning, or in accordance with the past generally.
ex: Sith thou gaue to vs a floure most riall Redolent in cronicles with historicall syght.

senses.d: Set in the past.
Former, erstwhile; (religious, obsolete) lapsed, nominal.
One of various tenses or moods used to tell about past events, historic (tense).
Synonym of hereditary or evolutionary.
Of, concerning, or in accordance with the scholarly discipline of history.
ex: The Royal Historical Society
The State Historical Society of Wisconsin

senses.d: Done in the manner of a historian: written as a development over time or in accordance with the historical method.
Synonym of historic: important or likely to be important to history and historians.
A historical romance.

senses.d: The aggregate of past events, both unrecorded and recorded.
ex: The history of mammals stretches back many millions of years.
History repeats itself if we don’t learn from its mistakes.

senses.d: The empirical study of past events, as distinct from literature, myth, or scripture; the assessment of notable events.
ex: He teaches Latin American history at the university and publishes books about the Cold War.

senses.d: The portion of the past that is known and recorded by this field of study, as opposed to all earlier and unknown times that preceded it.
ex: Near-synonym: ages
in all of human history and prehistory

senses.d: A set of events involving an entity.
ex: a long and sordid history
What is your medical history?

senses.d: A record or narrative description of past events.
ex: I really enjoyed Shakespeare's tragedies more than his histories.
a short history of post-Columbian colonization

senses.d: A list of past and continuing medical conditions of an individual or family.
ex: A personal medical history is required for the insurance policy.
He has a history of cancer in his family.

senses.d: A record of previous user events, especially of visited web pages in a browser.
ex: I visited a great site yesterday but forgot the URL. Luckily, I didn't clear my history.
When you do that, the browser window has no browser history, so it doesn't report a referrer page to the first site you visit.

senses.d: Something that no longer exists or is no longer relevant.
ex: I told him that if he doesn't get his act together, he's history.

senses.d: Shared experience or interaction.
ex: There is too much history between them for them to split up now.
He has had a lot of history with the police.

senses.d: A historically significant event.
ex: You are witnessing history!
We have a new president: Barack Obama. I never thought a black man would be elected. It's exciting! It's history!

senses.d: To narrate or record.
ex:
And therefore will hee wipe his Tables cleane,
And keepe no Tell-tale to his Memorie,
That may repeat, and Historie his losse
